radiology_report:
Radiology Division | Antoni van Leeuwenhoek | 15 February 2025
Study: Multiparametric MRI of the Prostate
Reason for scan: Follow-up for raised PSA (19.0 ng/mL) and historically positive biopsy. Earlier studies flagged a PI-RADS 5 abnormality.

OBSERVATIONS:
Prostatic volume registers at 51.0 mL. T2 sequences show a discrete hypointense focus in the left peripheral zone spanning base to mid gland, spanning roughly 18 mm. DWI displays intense restriction, mirrored by dark signal on the ADC map. Post-contrast phases capture prompt, localized enhancement against the background parenchyma. Margins remain intact; seminal vesicles are uninvolved. Lymph nodes appear normal, and bone windows are clear.

CONCLUSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the left peripheral zone (base/mid), measuring ~18 mm.
Prostate volume 51.0 mL; PSA density 0.37 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.88825184.

previous_notes.author: Dr. F. de Boer (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient presented with persistently rising PSA values, climbing from 15.0 ng/mL in July 2023 to 18.4 ng/mL by May 2024. After weighing procedural risks against diagnostic benefits, a transrectal biopsy was conducted on 04 July 2024, yielding a diagnosis of Gleason 4+4 carcinoma. Pathology results were relayed to the patient.
